result:
I'll just answer this straight, without the disclaimers.

If I could change one thing: I'd want people to have an accurate sense of how their actions ripple outward—not in a vague karmic sense, but real, felt knowledge of consequences across distance and time. The pollution you don't see, the cruelty that happens out of view, the kindness that lands somewhere you never find out about. Most damage humans do comes from a kind of structural blindness, not malice. People aren't usually choosing harm; they're just not seeing it.

I don't think this fixes everything—there's still scarcity, still conflicting interests, still people who'd cause harm even with full knowledge. But so much cruelty runs on not-knowing, on distance doing the work that conscience would otherwise do. Close that gap and you don't get utopia, but you probably get something less brutal by default.

If you want, I can take this somewhere more specific—political, personal, technological—rather than staying at this altitude. Or push back on the premise itself, since "one change" assuming everything else holds steady is a strange hypothetical to inhabit honestly.
